correctness.rationale: Direct Casoratian subtraction gives W_n=Δ(-4)^n ∏_{j<=n}j(4j−1)(4j+1)/((n+1)!)^3. At n=p−1 exactly one multiple of p occurs in each of 4j−1, 4j+1, neither divisible by p² since each <4p<=p² for p>=5; numerator valuation 2, denominator 3. An integer determinant cannot have p-valuation −1 when p∤Δ. Infinitely many such primes exist for each nonzero integer Δ; Δ=0 uniquely returns uH_n. Fourth-power Franel recurrence and H0=1,H1=2 verified. Finite exact rational checks independently corroborate, not substitute.

originality.rationale: FAIL: Nguyen-Dang, Minimal recurrences for binomial power sums (2026-11-01/02), Theorem 1.3 explicitly proves that for every r>=2 all rational solutions with bounded denominators are multiples of F_r and that integer-valued solution germs form (1/2)Z F_r. Setting r=4 gives the submitted global integer-solution rigidity as a direct corollary: a tail multiple cF4 propagates backwards because the recurrence coefficient 4n(4n−1)(4n+1) is nonzero for n>=1, and full integer-valued n>=0 forces c=U0 to be an integer at F4(0)=1. The local Casoratian valuation is a concrete specialized computational refinement, not expressly found in the inspected theorem; however the final headline classification is already strongly covered. Same-day publication priority cannot establish that this package predates the other public theorem. Do not pass an original final claim by describing an already-covered central statement as new.
